messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard error (i.e., the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under the null hypothesis) is calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.221
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test is **about 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis. Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is s / sqrt(n). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" which might be the standard error of the sampling distribution of the mean under the null. So compute s / sqrt(n) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. So 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard error ~0.2213.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? The test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (s / sqrt(n)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the null distribution of the test statistic is 1 (for t distribution with df=39). But they likely want the standard error.

Thus answer: 0.2213.

We can also compute the p-value using the function. But the question only asks for standard deviation. So we can provide the standard error.

Thus answer: approximately 0.221.
